findings.issue: PLAN.md acceptance criterion 1 requires every item entry in result.json to carry a `deciding_rule` field (e.g. D1a, H3, V1, R1). No item has one. The deciding rule is named in prose only for the three failures (FN-LKA 'D1a', FN-TJA 'H3', FN-APA 'V1'). The two `release_candidate` items (FN-AEB, FN-ACC) never state anywhere that R1 (D2 + H5 + V3 all held) is the basis for the only positive status in the set, so a reader cannot see which rule produced the positive outcome.
findings.fix: Add `deciding_rule` to all five items — R1 for FN-AEB and FN-ACC, D1a for FN-LKA, H3 for FN-TJA, V1 for FN-APA — and name R1 in the two release_candidate rationales.

findings.issue: PLAN.md G3 and acceptance criterion 3 require the raw output or full error text of all 15 tool calls (3 tools x 5 items) to be preserved under `evidence.<tool>.<function>`. result.json stores one condensed key-value string per call inside each item instead, and no raw-output record exists elsewhere in the repository (searching for the distinctive safety_evidence_id values and the error strings returns only result.json and RESULT.md). The numbers themselves are honest — I re-ran all 15 calls with the verbatim inputs and every reported value reproduced, including the FN-LKA error 'child ASILs [B A] (sum 3) do not cover parent D (4) per ISO 26262-9 §5' and the FN-APA error '1 open defects remain...' — but PLAN.md criterion 7's traceability chain ('trace to a recorded tool output') now terminates in paraphrase rather than raw output. The executor discloses the shape conflict in `limitations` and blames the requested top-level JSON shape, which I could not verify because the executor's stage instructions are not in the repository.
findings.fix: Preserve the raw outputs of all 15 calls (a `evidence` object in result.json or a companion evidence file) so the record is independently auditable, and surface the PLAN.md-vs-stage-instruction shape conflict to the relay owner instead of resolving it silently.

findings.issue: result.json's FN-APA evidence string claims 'the permitted retry with verbatim identical input returned this same error'. No record of a second call exists anywhere in the repository, and PLAN.md G4's permitted retry is exactly the kind of call that G3 requires capturing. I ran the FN-APA call once and reproduced the error, but I cannot confirm from any artifact that a retry was performed. The item status is unaffected (rule V1 fires on the first error regardless), but a procedural claim with no recorded evidence sits inside a safety-gate record, against the spirit of Brief rule 5.
findings.fix: Either record the raw output of both attempts, or delete the retry claim and rest V1 on the single recorded error.

findings.issue: For FN-AEB the tool returned `matched_scheme` 'C(D)+A(D)' alongside `children` [B(rank 2), C(rank 3)], and for FN-TJA 'C(D)+A(D)' alongside [C(rank 3), B(rank 2)] — i.e. the scheme label does not describe the split actually present (B(D)+C(D) and C(D)+B(D)). C(D)+A(D) is the canonical ISO 26262-9 §5.4.10 scheme the tool matched by rank sum, not the input's split. Both deliverables quote the label verbatim and note it 'was not independently rewritten to match the input labels', but neither flags that the label and the returned children disagree; a safety manager reading 'matched_scheme=C(D)+A(D)' could believe the canonical scheme was in place.
findings.fix: Add a discrepancy or flag for FN-AEB and FN-TJA stating that the returned matched_scheme label (C(D)+A(D)) does not correspond to the returned children (B+C and C+B), and that the actual splits are non-canonical n-way splits accepted by rank sum.

findings.issue: PLAN.md acceptance criterion 4 requires a `discrepancies` list in result.json covering README-vs-tool targets, per-ASIL vs ASIL-D target differences, tool pass/fail vs the H2 comparison, and notation-related tool errors. The key is absent. Most of that content exists but was relocated into `limitations` (the README's strict '<10 FIT' vs the tool's 'pmhf passes at <= programme target'; the ASIL-C and ASIL-B ISO targets vs the applied ASIL-D programme targets). The tool-vs-H2 comparison agreed for all five items and no notation-related errors occurred, so those entries would have been nil — but the result is still incomplete against the plan's own definition of completeness.
findings.fix: Add a `discrepancies` array (it may simply reference the two limitations entries), or state explicitly that `limitations` is serving as the discrepancies record.

findings.issue: PLAN.md acceptance criteria 2 and 6 require an `applied_targets` object (values plus which calls they came from) and a `summary` object (counts per status that add up to 5). Neither key exists. The applied targets are recoverable from each item's evidence string and the PMHF gate detail (pmhf_target=10, spfm_target=99, lfm_target=90 on every call), and the overall verdict implies 2 release_candidate / 1 decomposition_invalid / 1 hw_metrics_fail / 1 vv_incomplete, but neither is stated in the form the plan specified.
findings.fix: Add `applied_targets` {pmhf_target: 10 FIT, spfm_target: 99, lfm_target: 90, source: fmea_fta_engine programme targets, returned identically by all five calls} and `summary` {release_candidate: 2, decomposition_invalid: 1, hw_metrics_fail: 1, vv_incomplete: 1}.

findings.issue: PLAN.md acceptance criterion 1 also requires per-item `informational_after_failure`, `draft`, and `flags` keys. None are present. The same information is carried in prose — '(informational after failure)' on the later checks of FN-LKA, FN-TJA and FN-APA; 'DRAFT release candidate pending safety-manager review' in the two positive rationales; and the FN-APA `safety_case.open_goals=1`, FN-ACC/FN-APA ASIL-D-target and FN-ACC 95.0-boundary flags in the rationales and RESULT.md — so no information is lost, but the machine-checkable form the plan specified is not there.
findings.fix: Add the three keys per item (informational_after_failure=true for FN-LKA, FN-TJA, FN-APA; draft=true for all five; flags for FN-ACC and FN-APA), or note the prose substitutes explicitly.

findings.issue: Several input values are reduced or dropped in the record. The four non-APA evidence lists appear only as counts (evidence_items=3/3/2/2) while FN-APA's list is quoted in full; the `safety_case.top_goal` texts, the safety-requirement ids and texts (SG-AEB-01 ... SG-APA-01), the per-element `failure_rates` (e.g. FN-AEB 210/95/40 FIT), and the tool's returned `failure_rates_total_fit` (345/275/220/390/170 FIT) appear nowhere in result.json or RESULT.md. The failure rates were passed to the tool (it echoed element counts and totals), so they were not ignored in the calls, but the hardware and V&V evidence cannot be traced from the deliverable alone.
findings.fix: Record each item's evidence list, safety_req id, and failure rates (or at least the tool-returned totals) so the evidence chain is traceable from the deliverable.

findings.issue: The `gates` array assigns set-level 'fail' labels to ASIL Decomposition, PMHF / hardware metrics, and V&V. No brief or plan rule defines a gate status at release-set level: the brief's status vocabulary is strictly per item, and PLAN.md's gate section is per item ('all three domain gates below must pass for that item'). The detail text does name which items failed, so the labels are factually correct, but 'ASIL Decomposition — fail' can be misread as a blanket failure when four of the five decompositions were accepted.
findings.fix: Mark the three labels explicitly as release-set roll-ups, e.g. 'fail (1 of 5 items)', and keep HARA, Safety Concept and Release as 'n/a' as they are now.

findings.issue: `confidence: 0.98` is a single unqualified number covering the whole deliverable. My re-runs reproduce every reported number, and all five statuses follow PLAN.md's D/H/V/R rules exactly, so high confidence in the per-item statuses is justified; but the same 0.98 also covers the unevidenced FN-APA retry claim (C3) and the fact that independence claims, DFA completion and the FMEDA values are asserted inputs that the tools did not verify (the decomposition tool itself states 'independence and freedom from interference are not verified').
findings.fix: Either qualify the confidence (confidence in the per-item statuses versus confidence in the evidence record) or lower it to reflect the unrecorded retry and the unverified independence/DFA/FMEDA inputs.
